To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the absorption coefficient of the semiconductor is time-dependent and that the nonlinear absorption of the CO2 laser pulse in a semiconductor is determined by the intensity of the pulse and its duration.

the nonlinear absorption in InSb is caused by the generation of electron-hole pairs by the laser radiation and that the time dependence of the nonlinear absorption is determined by the time dependence of this generation.
nonlinear absorption of a randomly pulsating CO 2 laser pulse in InAs can be described by an equation that includes time-dependent parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nonlinear interaction of radiation with matter, which is of fundamental and technological importance.
nonlinear absorption in narrow-gap semiconsuctors under the action of a CO2 laser pulse operating in random pulsation or in a mode-locked condition.
the study of the nonlinear absorption in narrow-gap semicolloids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a CO2 laser pulse of 0.5 J, the nonlinear absorption coefficient is of the order of 0.1 to 1.0 cm−1, and the nonlinear refraction coefficient is of the same order of magnitude.
the transmission of the CO2 laser radiation is determined by the time-averaged nonlinear absorption of the radiation.

the transmission of the laser radiation by the InAs samples under random pulsation and mode locking conditions is due to the time-dependent nonlinear absorption in the material, and this time dependence is due to the interaction between the radiation and the carriers in the semiconductor material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear optical absorption in semiconductors is a function of the intensity of the incident radiation, the time of the incident pulse, the temperature of the semiconductor, and the wavelength.
we have demonstrated a new nonlinear optical effect, namely time-dependent nonlinear absorption, which is a result of a competition between nonlinear absorption and self-focusing.

the nonlinear absorption of randomly pulsated CO2 laser radiation by InAs is a function of the intensity of the incident radiation, the time duration of the incident pulse, the repetition rate of the incident pulses, the temperature of the semiconductor, the thickness of the sample, and the wavelength of the incident laser radiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time-dependent nonlinear absorption of randomly pulsation CO2 laser radiation by narrow-gap semiconoductors is much stronger than the nonlinear absorption of mode-locked CO2 laser radiation.
the transmission of the laser radiation by a semiconductor sample depends on the intensity of the radiation and its pulse duration.
the nonlinear optical response is a very useful tool for studying the physical processes that occur in semiconductors and other materials.
